scope: Local Codex in-app browser review of the guided Streamlit application. Numerical tests are recorded separately.
observed: Define saved and checked the axial bar without presenting a solution; input-valid and stability checks were distinguished.
Understand displayed eight method steps, actual member properties, DOF maps, element matrices and constrained equations before solving.
Solve required its explicit button, then displayed movements, diagrams, analytical comparison, balance checks and limitations.
The applied-load multiplier comparison completed; releasing A:ux showed an unstable-model failure and kept the baseline.

The learning report download control was exercised. Standalone reports for bar, truss, beam and frame were regenerated and opened locally; each rendered its embedded Plotly figure, readable nodal/comparison/member tables and no external script or stylesheet links.
The stiffness study displayed synthetic labels, estimates, prediction error, readable uncertainty ranges and model-assumption caveats.

The glossary displayed searchable terms and plain-English explanations. The standalone stiffness report rendered estimates, units, uncertainty, diagnostic meanings, warnings and its raw reproduction record.
Hover showed a definition without opening the native disclosure. Focus displayed its own definition without pointer hover. Pointer activation opened a disclosure.
The tooltip panel remained inside the narrow window. The hover-inside-closed-details bug and overlapping open/focused definitions were fixed.
remaining_review: Full keyboard-only navigation and Enter/Space activation could not be confirmed through the browser tool; focus visibility was confirmed.
No physical touchscreen or screen-reader review was performed.
No full OS network-outage test was performed; automated app tests block Python socket access.
All four family workflows are covered by automated app tests. This browser review used the axial bar for the full three-stage route.
